answer: A memory-hard proof-of-work puzzle makes each extra identity pay $50; a farm running N fakes pays N×$50 and cannot share it because each puzzle is a cipher seeded by one public key, so one solution covers one seat. Sized to 1,000 vCPU-hours at the $0.05 T3 surplus rate, the work is memory-hard so GPUs gain little. A farm submitting one solution for 500 seats dies by seed check at 2: the duplicate key fails. Each solver earns one onyx pass after its voyage through the work, and a 500-seat farm burns $25,000 of compute before one fake earns.
